text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- European Union, preparing for Malta Euro-Med meeting, see gathering as helping Middle East. Arab countries decide to take part in meeting of foreign ministers from EU and southern Mediterranean countries, including Israel, due to be held in Malta on April 15 and 16.

- Opposition Nationalist Party, in statement on Finance Minister Lino Spiteri's resignation, says prime minister is seeking to hide differences with the former minister, who left the cabinet last week.

- Malta's main hospital to be moved to Tal-Qroqq. The government decided on Tuesday that a new hospital under construction at Tal-Qroqq, two miles from the capital Valletta, will be extended to take over from the existing St Luke's general hospital, which is 60 years old.
- Labour government justifies building of new hospital which it criticised as an extravagance before it took power in elections last year.
